chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about fasting in the month, how is it? He said: 'Three [days] in the month, in each ten-day period one day, for indeed Allah, Exalted and Glorious, says: "Whoever comes with a good deed will have ten like it." And three days in the month are the fasting of a lifetime.'
This fasting is voluntary (nafl) and supererogatory (tatawwu'), so how is its ordering? And that which indicates what we mentioned is what he narrated:

key_terms.التَّنَفُّل: Voluntary prayer or fasting performed in addition to obligatory acts
key_terms.صَوْمُ الدَّهْرِ: Fasting of a lifetime (continuous or equivalent reward)
key_terms.عَشْرُ أَمْثَالِهَا: Ten times its like (referring to the reward multiplier)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for fasting three days a month in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) elucidates the spiritual magnitude of the *Ayyam al-Beed* (white days), linking the specific reward of tenfold multiplication to the concept that three days equate to a lifetime of fasting. This highlights the Shia emphasis on *Sawm al-Tatawwu'* (voluntary fasting) as a means of spiritual refinement and reward accumulation, distinct from obligatory duties. The text serves as a foundational proof for the merit of consistent, moderate voluntary worship within the lunar calendar.
